text:
anna: Quick heads-up — I'm sketching a change to how we enforce model-family quotas. Current slab/burst model works but spikes from a few noisy keys blow out tail latency. Proposal: add token-smoothing + small reservation pool per model family + an exponential penalty that temporarily reduces burst allowance if a key repeatedly spikes. Want quick feedback before an RFC.

mike: sounds promising. can you show a sample config?

anna: sure — rough idea below:
```yaml
families:
  - name: gptx-8k
    steady_rate_tokens_per_sec: 1200   # aggregated across org
    max_burst_tokens: 10000
    smoothing_window_ms: 60000         # moving-average window used to smooth burst accounting
    reservation_pct: 0.03             # small reserved pool for short high-priority bursts
    penalty_backoff_seconds: 180      # exponential backoff window after penalty triggers
```

raj: couple of thoughts: 1) smoothing_window ties in tightly with our prefix cache behavior — shorter windows favor latency, longer windows favor cost. we should expose as per-family tuning. 2) reservation_pct — how do we prevent reservation hogging?

anna: my thought: reservations are only usable when a request would otherwise be throttled; they are metered and show up in telemetry. if a key uses >50% of reserved pool in 60s, apply soft penalty (drop future reservation access for that key for penalty_backoff_seconds).

sophia: curious about enforcement point — gateway vs serving nodes? gateway is easiest but we lose model-aware knowledge there. serving nodes can make smarter decisions (sequence length, kv cache reuse).

mike: we should keep enforcement at gateway for fast fail and global accounting, but let serving runtime accept a token-cookie that indicates a reservation was consumed so we can prefer that connection for lower queue reorder penalties. basically two-layer enforcement.

raj: makes sense. also: metrics — we need a few new time-series: family.smoothing_rate, family.reservation_used, key.penalty_count, key.current_backoff. add labels: family, org, key_type (api_key vs token).

anna: agreed. dashboards: plot reservation consumption as a heatmap across families and top 50 keys. console should allow quick drilling into a key to see its history and penalty events.

console-bot: new dashboard "Family Quota Smoothing" created in staging under Observability > Quotas — includes heatmap + per-key penalty timeline.

mike: edge case: short high-throughput bursts using many short requests (chat stream chunking). smoothing based on tokens/sec might undercount because each chunk creates overhead. Maybe we should compute an amortized tokens-per-request using median sequence length per key.

anna: good call. we already have per-route seq len histograms. we can feed a per-key median_seq_len into the smoothing algorithm to normalize. pseudocode:
```python
# smoothing on arrival
weight = median_seq_len_for_key(key) / global_median_len
adj_tokens = incoming_tokens * weight
smoothed = ema(key_window_ms, adj_tokens)
if smoothed > family_threshold: throttle_or_consume_reservation()
```

raj: how will this interact with model-variant fallbacks? if family has small quantized variants for cheap capacity, do we count them against the same family limit?

anna: yes same family. but we allow routing policy to downgrade model variant without touching quota accounting (i.e., the tokens still count). fallback is only routing change. if a key is penalized, routing should prefer cheaper variants for that key until penalty expires.

sophia: UX question: when a key gets penalized, we should surface that in the console with an explanation and ETA for penalty expiry. otherwise customers will be confused. show an example message in CLI/API response?

anna: propose returning 429 with structured body: {"reason": "family_quota_penalty", "family": "gptx-8k", "penalty_expires_at": "2026-11-05T12:34:56Z", "can_reserve": false}. makes it debuggable and actionable.

mike: +1. maybe add a hint: "try model: gptx-8k-lite for degraded throughput" so SDKs can auto-fallback.

raj: telemetry retention — we need to keep penalty events longer (90d) for billing disputes. add audit log entry per penalty with reason + sample requests.

anna: noted — will include audit events. also we should consider per-org override toggles for high-tier customers (reserved slices rather than reservations).

deploy-bot: rate-limiter: updated smoothing prototype deployed to staging at 2026-03-18T15:22:10Z, config path: /configs/rl/smoothing/v1. Running canary on 5% of traffic (org ids starting with 0a).

mike: can we run a synthetic workload that simulates noisy keys? i'll throw together a k6 script.

anna: thanks — if canary looks good i'll open RFC for API semantics and console flows. aim to keep defaults conservative (low reservation_pct, longer smoothing window) to avoid surprising users.

sophia: +1. also add a console toggle to "show penalty events" and an email alert subscription for high severity penalties.

raj: quick nit: name it token-smoothing + reservation + penalty? maybe shorthand "smoothed-burst-control".

anna: I like "smoothed-burst-control" for the RFC. i'll update the staging dashboard with example keys and grab baseline metrics.

console-bot: dashboard widget updated with sample keys and synthetic canary overlay.

mike: :thumbsup: i'll post k6 results here when ready.

anna: thanks all — filing RFC Monday unless objections.

mike: none from me.

raj: go for it."
